meta.title: Lumentum Holdings — the JDSU-spin optical components vendor through the 800G datacom transceiver cycle and the AI infrastructure inflection
meta.abstract: Lumentum Holdings was carved out of JDS Uniphase in August 2015 to separate the optical communications and commercial laser businesses from JDSU's network test product line (which became Viavi Solutions). The optical communications segment serves the telecom and datacom transceiver markets through ROADMs, tunable lasers, indium phosphide chips, and pluggable optical modules; the commercial laser segment serves industrial materials processing, semiconductor manufacturing, and 3D sensing applications. The 2018-2020 period was defined by the Oclaro acquisition completing the indium phosphide vertical integration and by the Apple 3D sensing VCSEL revenue scaling. The 2022-2024 period saw the telecom market downturn compress the legacy network equipment exposure while the datacom transceiver market began scaling on the AI infrastructure cycle. Under CEO Michael Hurlston (joined February 2024 from Synaptics), the strategic focus has shifted decisively toward the 800G and 1.6T datacom transceiver opportunity at hyperscaler customers, with cloud-and-datacenter revenue becoming the largest single growth driver. The 2023 NeoPhotonics acquisition (closed August 2022) added coherent transceiver technology and additional hyperscaler customer relationships. Fiscal 2025 quarterly progression has demonstrated the cloud-and-datacenter scaling continuing while the telecom segment stabilises off the post-cycle bottom; the multi-year AI infrastructure cycle provides the structural demand context for the optical interconnect transition.

chapters.title: Snapshot
chapters.body:
## A Decade in the Making

Lumentum's AI-era inflection did not arrive as a brand-new business. It arrived as a repricing of capabilities the company had been assembling for years: indium phosphide device manufacturing, coherent optics know-how, and, after Cloud Light, a much broader module and packaging footprint. By fiscal 2025, that architecture was finally visible in the numbers. Revenue rose to $1,645.0 million from $1,359.2 million a year earlier, and management said the outperformance was broad-based across its cloud-focused business, with particular strength in EML chips, pump lasers, narrow-linewidth laser assemblies, and 800G modules. [Lumentum Q4 FY2025 results](https://investor.lumentum.com/financial-news-releases/news-details/2025/Lumentum-Announces-Fourth-Quarter-and-Full-Fiscal-Year-2025-Results/default.aspx) [FY2025 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1633978/000162828025040830/lite-20250628.htm)

Lumentum Holdings Inc. was incorporated by JDS Uniphase on February 10, 2015 and became an independent public company in August 2015, when JDSU distributed the shares and the remaining parent was renamed Viavi Solutions. The company remained headquartered in San Jose, California, but the operating footprint that mattered by the frozen window was much broader: fabs in Japan, the United States and the United Kingdom, and large-scale assembly and test operations in Thailand. [FY2025 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1633978/000162828025040830/lite-20250628.htm) [2025 proxy statement](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1633978/000130817925000615/lite014752-def14a.htm)

Leadership changed at precisely the point the revenue curve turned. On February 3, 2025, Lumentum announced that Michael Hurlston would succeed Alan Lowe as president, chief executive officer and a director, effective February 7. Hurlston came from Synaptics, where he had served as chief executive since 2019; before that he had run Finisar and had spent November 2001 to October 2017 at Broadcom in a series of senior operating roles. The board's case for the change, laid out more fully in the 2025 proxy, was that Lumentum needed a chief executive with direct photonics-industry experience and a record of portfolio repositioning. [Leadership transition release](https://investor.lumentum.com/financial-news-releases/news-details/2025/Lumentum-Announces-Leadership-Transition/default.aspx) [2025 proxy statement](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1633978/000130817925000615/lite014752-def14a.htm)

## Two Segments, One Growth Engine

By fiscal 2025 Lumentum reported two segments: Cloud & Networking and Industrial Tech. The first generated $1,410.8 million of revenue, or 85.8 percent of the group total, while Industrial Tech generated $234.2 million. That split mattered because it showed how far the company had moved from its earlier balance between telecom optics, consumer sensing, and industrial lasers. Cloud & Networking was no longer simply the larger segment; it had become the center of gravity. [FY2025 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1633978/000162828025040830/lite-20250628.htm)

The acquisitive sequence that produced that mix unfolded in three steps. Lumentum agreed in March 2018 to buy Oclaro for approximately $1.8 billion in cash and stock and closed the transaction in December 2018, adding Oclaro's indium phosphide and coherent-component portfolio. In November 2021 it agreed to buy NeoPhotonics for $16.00 a share, or approximately $918 million in equity value, and closed that acquisition on August 3, 2022. Then, on October 30, 2023, it announced a roughly $750 million acquisition of Cloud Light; when the deal closed on November 7, 2023, the purchase-price consideration recorded by Lumentum was $728.5 million, with $705.0 million of cash paid at closing. [Oclaro acquisition announcement](https://investor.lumentum.com/financial-news-releases/news-details/2018/Lumentum-To-Acquire-Oclaro-For-1-8B-In-Cash-And-Stock-2018-3-12/default.aspx) [Oclaro acquisition close](https://investor.lumentum.com/financial-news-releases/news-details/2018/Lumentum-Announces-Completion-Of-Oclaro-Acquisition-2018-12-10/default.aspx) [NeoPhotonics acquisition announcement](https://investor.lumentum.com/financial-news-releases/news-details/2021/Lumentum-To-Acquire-NeoPhotonics-to-Accelerate-Optical-Network-Speed-And-Scalability/default.aspx) [NeoPhotonics acquisition close](https://investor.lumentum.com/financial-news-releases/news-details/2022/Lumentum-Announces-Completion-of-NeoPhotonics-Acquisition/default.aspx) [Cloud Light announcement](https://investor.lumentum.com/financial-news-releases/news-details/2023/Lumentum-to-Acquire-Cloud-Light-to-Accelerate-Data-Center-Speed-and-Scalability/default.aspx) [Q2 FY2024 results](https://investor.lumentum.com/financial-news-releases/news-details/2024/Lumentum-Announces-Fiscal-Second-Quarter-2024-Financial-Results/)

## From Trough to Inflection

The starting point for the Hurlston era was still a trough. Fiscal 2024 revenue fell to $1,359.2 million from $1,767.0 million in fiscal 2023. The company attributed the decline to weaker telecom demand and lower imaging-and-sensing sales, while the FY2024 filing and the 2025 proxy both showed how concentrated the business remained during the downcycle. Fiscal 2025 marked the first clear reversal: revenue rose 21.0 percent to $1,645.0 million, non-GAAP operating margin reached 9.7 percent, and Cloud & Networking supplied nearly all of the growth. [FY2024 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1633978/000162828024038024/lite-20240629.htm) [FY2025 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1633978/000162828025040830/lite-20250628.htm) [2025 proxy statement](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1633978/000130817925000615/lite014752-def14a.htm)

| Period | Total revenue | Selected supporting detail |
|---|---:|---|
| FY2024 | $1,359.2m | Cloud & Networking $1,084.9m; Industrial Tech $274.3m |
| FY2025 | $1,645.0m | Cloud & Networking $1,410.8m; Industrial Tech $234.2m |
| Q4 FY2025 | $480.7m | Non-GAAP gross margin 37.8% |
| Q1 FY2026 | $533.8m | Components $379.2m; Systems $154.6m |
| Q2 FY2026 | $665.5m | Non-GAAP gross margin 42.5% |
| Q3 FY2026 | $808.4m | Components $533.3m; Systems $275.1m |

The progression after fiscal 2025 showed the cloud build-out scaling quarter by quarter rather than in a single burst. Q1 FY2026 revenue was $533.8 million, Q2 FY2026 revenue was $665.5 million, and Q3 FY2026 revenue was $808.4 million. By the March 2026 quarter, Lumentum's cash, cash equivalents and short-term investments had risen to $3,172.3 million, up $2,017.0 million sequentially, primarily because of the March 2026 issuance of Series A Convertible Preferred Stock. [Q4 FY2025 results](https://investor.lumentum.com/financial-news-releases/news-details/2025/Lumentum-Announces-Fourth-Quarter-and-Full-Fiscal-Year-2025-Results/default.aspx) [Q1 FY2026 results](https://investor.lumentum.com/financial-news-releases/news-details/2025/Lumentum-Announces-First-Quarter-of-Fiscal-Year-2026-Financial-Results/default.aspx) [Q2 FY2026 results](https://investor.lumentum.com/financial-news-releases/news-details/2026/Lumentum-Announces-Second-Quarter-of-Fiscal-Year-2026-Financial-Results/default.aspx) [Q3 FY2026 results](https://investor.lumentum.com/financial-news-releases/news-details/2026/Lumentum-Announces-Third-Quarter-of-Fiscal-Year-2026-Financial-Results/default.aspx)

## The EML Chokepoint

The clearest through-line in Lumentum's official materials was not a claimed market-share figure; it was the way the company kept tying revenue acceleration to lasers and modules at the heart of AI-cluster interconnect. In November 2024, Alan Lowe said the company had set a new record for datacom laser-chip orders, including substantial 200G EML orders. In August 2025, Hurlston said fiscal Q4 outperformance was driven by EML chips, pump lasers, narrow-linewidth laser assemblies and 800G modules. In February 2026, he said two newer growth engines - optical circuit switches and co-packaged optics - were still only at their starting line, even as OCS backlog had already moved beyond $400 million and the company had received an incremental multi-hundred-million-dollar co-packaged-optics order deliverable in the first half of calendar 2027. [Q1 FY2025 results](https://investor.lumentum.com/financial-news-releases/news-details/2024/Lumentum-Announces-Fiscal-First-Quarter-2025-Financial-Results/) [Q4 FY2025 results](https://investor.lumentum.com/financial-news-releases/news-details/2025/Lumentum-Announces-Fourth-Quarter-and-Full-Fiscal-Year-2025-Results/default.aspx) [Q2 FY2026 results](https://investor.lumentum.com/financial-news-releases/news-details/2026/Lumentum-Announces-Second-Quarter-of-Fiscal-Year-2026-Financial-Results/default.aspx)

The hardware roadmap backed up that narrative. Lumentum's own product pages showed 100G and 200G PAM4 EMLs for 400G, 800G and 1.6T pluggables; 800G 2xDR4 direct-detect modules built on silicon photonics and four 1311 nm CW DFB lasers; and 800G ZR+ coherent pluggables that combined indium phosphide photonic integrated circuits with silicon photonics. By the spring of 2026, the company was also publicly showing a 1.6T DR4 OSFP prototype using four 400G differential EMLs as a stepping-stone to 3.2T. [EML 100G product page](https://www.lumentum.com/en/products/eml-100g-pam4-cwdm-laser) [EML 200G product page](https://www.lumentum.com/en/products/eml-200g-pam4-cwdm-laser) [800G 2xDR4 OSFP](https://www.lumentum.com/en/products/800g-2dr4-osfp-transceiver-module) [800G ZR+ coherent pluggables](https://www.lumentum.com/en/products/800g-zr-coherent-pluggable-transceivers) [OFC 2026 release](https://investor.lumentum.com/financial-news-releases/news-details/2026/Lumentum-Demonstrates-Industry-Leading-Technologies-and-Products-for-Scale-Out-Scale-Up-and-Scale-Across-AI-Infrastructure-at-OFC-2026/default.aspx)

## What the Dossier Asks

The central questions entering the frozen window were therefore more concrete than the original draft sometimes implied. The first was whether AI-linked optical demand would stay strong enough to absorb the capacity being added across components, modules, optical circuit switches and co-packaged optics. The second was whether Lumentum could turn its three-step build-out - Oclaro, NeoPhotonics, Cloud Light - into a durable margin structure rather than a brief scarcity premium. The third was whether Industrial Tech would remain a useful second earnings leg while Cloud & Networking continued to dominate the story. Those are the threads the rest of the dossier follows. [Q2 FY2026 results](https://investor.lumentum.com/financial-news-releases/news-details/2026/Lumentum-Announces-Second-Quarter-of-Fiscal-Year-2026-Financial-Results/default.aspx) [Q3 FY2026 results](https://investor.lumentum.com/financial-news-releases/news-details/2026/Lumentum-Announces-Third-Quarter-of-Fiscal-Year-2026-Financial-Results/default.aspx)

---

*Primary sources used in this chapter: Lumentum investor relations releases, the FY2024 and FY2025 Forms 10-K, the FY2026 Q1-Q3 earnings releases, and the 2025 proxy statement.*


What changed in the spring of 2026 was that several validation loops closed at once. Q2 FY2026 said OCS backlog had moved beyond $400 million and disclosed an incremental multi-hundred-million-dollar co-packaged-optics order for the first half of calendar 2027. On March 2, NVIDIA announced a $2 billion strategic investment and multibillion purchase commitment. On March 23, Lumentum joined the S&P 500, and by May 18 it had joined the Nasdaq-100. The Greensboro manufacturing announcement then tied those market and balance-sheet milestones to a concrete capacity plan. [Q2 FY2026 results](https://investor.lumentum.com/financial-news-releases/news-details/2026/Lumentum-Announces-Second-Quarter-of-Fiscal-Year-2026-Financial-Results/default.aspx) [NVIDIA-Lumentum partnership](https://investor.lumentum.com/financial-news-releases/news-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Strategic-Partnership-With-Lumentum-to-Develop-State-of-the-Art-Optics-Technology/default.aspx) [S&P 500 release](https://investor.lumentum.com/financial-news-releases/news-details/2026/Lumentum-to-Join-the-SP-500-Index/default.aspx) [Greensboro facility release](https://investor.lumentum.com/financial-news-releases/news-details/2026/Lumentum-Announces-New-U-S--Manufacturing-Facility-to-Produce-Advanced-Lasers-for-the-Worlds-Largest-AI-Data-Centers/default.aspx) [Lumentum company timeline](https://www.lumentum.com/en/company)

That was why the company looked different by the end of the frozen window than it had a year earlier. The market was not only paying for strong quarterly shipments. It was paying for the possibility that Lumentum had become one of the few optical suppliers with the balance sheet, manufacturing footprint and product breadth to matter across the next several interconnect transitions at once.

chapters.title: From the August 2015 JDSU spin through Oclaro, NeoPhotonics, and Hurlston
chapters.body:
## The JDSU Spin-Off and the Standalone Lumentum

Lumentum's corporate starting point was laid out plainly in the FY2025 Form 10-K. JDS Uniphase created the subsidiary on February 10, 2015, spun it off in August of that year, and then renamed the remaining parent Viavi Solutions. What sat inside the new Lumentum was the optical-networking and laser portfolio rather than the network-test franchise. The company therefore entered the market not as a venture-backed newcomer but as a carved-out photonics operation with manufacturing depth, customer programs and a public-company inheritance from the old JDSU franchise. [FY2025 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1633978/000162828025040830/lite-20250628.htm)

That distinction mattered because it shaped the first decade's mandate. Alan Lowe led the company from the spin until the 2025 succession, and the board's transition release later described his tenure as spanning the separation, the acquisitions that followed, and the shift into cloud optics. In practical terms, the early Lumentum story was about proving that a focused optical-and-laser supplier could create steadier value than the broader conglomerate from which it had been separated. [Leadership transition release](https://investor.lumentum.com/financial-news-releases/news-details/2025/Lumentum-Announces-Leadership-Transition/default.aspx) [FY2025 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1633978/000162828025040830/lite-20250628.htm)

The early revenue trajectory captured that first phase of independence: $1,247.7 million in fiscal 2018, $1,565.3 million in fiscal 2019, $1,678.6 million in fiscal 2020, and $1,742.8 million in fiscal 2021. Those years combined telecom and datacom optics with commercial and sensing lasers before later acquisitions and the AI cycle changed the mix more decisively. [FY2020 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1633978/000163397820000011/lumentumfy20-10k.htm) [2024 proxy statement](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1633978/000130817924000748/lite4368861_def14a.htm)

## The Consumer 3D-Sensing Supercycle

One of the decisive turns in Lumentum's history came not from telecom operators but from consumer 3D sensing. Lumentum's own company timeline said its VCSEL technology entered volume production for 3D sensing in consumer applications in 2017, and by March 2026 the company was describing that manufacturing base as having shipped more than 10 billion emitters. The consumer-sensing ramp therefore was not a side venture. It became a scaled manufacturing franchise that later informed the company's thinking about adjacent optical architectures. [Lumentum company timeline](https://www.lumentum.com/en/company) [VCSEL scale-up release](https://investor.lumentum.com/financial-news-releases/news-details/2026/Lumentum-Showcases-Breakthrough-Optical-Scale-Up-Demonstration-at-OFC-2026-Using-VCSEL-Technology/default.aspx)

| Fiscal year | Revenue |
|---|---:|
| FY2018 | $1,247.7m |
| FY2019 | $1,565.3m |
| FY2020 | $1,678.6m |
| FY2021 | $1,742.8m |
| FY2022 | $1,712.6m |
| FY2023 | $1,767.0m |
| FY2024 | $1,359.2m |
| FY2025 | $1,645.0m |

That table described more than a simple growth arc. It described the shape of a concentration problem. Revenue surged as consumer 3D sensing scaled, then flattened and ultimately fell back as that demand normalized and telecom spending weakened at the same time. The FY2024 and FY2025 filings explicitly pointed to imaging-and-sensing softness as part of the explanation for the trough. In hindsight, the consumer-sensing era financed and stress-tested capabilities that mattered later, but it also taught management how exposed the company could become when one end market did too much of the work. [FY2024 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1633978/000162828024038024/lite-20240629.htm) [FY2025 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1633978/000162828025040830/lite-20250628.htm)

## Oclaro and the InP Build-Out

Lumentum's first large strategic answer was Oclaro. On March 12, 2018, the company announced an agreement to acquire Oclaro for approximately $1.8 billion in cash and stock, describing the deal as a way to strengthen its indium phosphide laser, photonic-integrated-circuit and coherent-component capabilities. The acquisition closed on December 10, 2018. That chronology mattered because it separated the strategic promise from the operating reality: March was when management told investors what it wanted to become; December was when the manufacturing, engineering and product assets actually came inside the company. [Oclaro acquisition announcement](https://investor.lumentum.com/financial-news-releases/news-details/2018/Lumentum-To-Acquire-Oclaro-For-1-8B-In-Cash-And-Stock-2018-3-12/default.aspx) [Oclaro acquisition close](https://investor.lumentum.com/financial-news-releases/news-details/2018/Lumentum-Announces-Completion-Of-Oclaro-Acquisition-2018-12-10/default.aspx)

The enduring significance of Oclaro was that it deepened Lumentum's indium-phosphide and coherent portfolio at exactly the part of the optical stack where later AI-datacenter demand would become most supply-constrained. By the FY2025 10-K and the 2025 proxy, management was describing a company with fabs in Japan, the United States and the United Kingdom and with scaled assembly and test operations in Thailand. That footprint did not emerge all at once, but Oclaro was the transaction that made Lumentum look less like a collection of product lines and more like a vertically integrated photonics manufacturer. [2025 proxy statement](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1633978/000130817925000615/lite014752-def14a.htm) [FY2025 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1633978/000162828025040830/lite-20250628.htm)

## NeoPhotonics and Cloud Light

The second major deal was NeoPhotonics. Lumentum announced the acquisition on November 4, 2021 at $16.00 a share, or roughly $918 million in equity value, and closed it on August 3, 2022 after the needed approvals arrived. The official transaction language emphasized higher-speed optical components for cloud and telecom infrastructure and more than $50 million of expected annual run-rate cost synergies within 24 months. More importantly for the later dossier, NeoPhotonics added coherent optics depth and engineering talent that sat naturally inside the cloud-and-networking roadmap that emerged in 2025 and 2026. [NeoPhotonics acquisition announcement](https://investor.lumentum.com/financial-news-releases/news-details/2021/Lumentum-To-Acquire-NeoPhotonics-to-Accelerate-Optical-Network-Speed-And-Scalability/default.aspx) [NeoPhotonics acquisition close](https://investor.lumentum.com/financial-news-releases/news-details/2022/Lumentum-Announces-Completion-of-NeoPhotonics-Acquisition/default.aspx)

The third deal, Cloud Light, shifted the emphasis from chips and subsystems toward packaging and finished optical connectivity. The October 30, 2023 announcement valued the transaction at approximately $750 million, subject to adjustments, and said Cloud Light had generated more than $200 million of revenue in the prior 12 months, with over half of its most recent-quarter optical-transceiver revenue coming from 800G modules. When the closing was reflected in Lumentum's quarter-end accounting a week later, the purchase-price consideration recorded was $728.5 million. That difference was not cosmetic. It underscored that the deal moved from narrative to balance-sheet fact almost immediately. [Cloud Light announcement](https://investor.lumentum.com/financial-news-releases/news-details/2023/Lumentum-to-Acquire-Cloud-Light-to-Accelerate-Data-Center-Speed-and-Scalability/default.aspx) [Q2 FY2024 results](https://investor.lumentum.com/financial-news-releases/news-details/2024/Lumentum-Announces-Fiscal-Second-Quarter-2024-Financial-Results/)

Seen in sequence, the three turning points were different in kind. Oclaro strengthened the InP and coherent manufacturing core. NeoPhotonics deepened the coherent and cloud-networking design stack. Cloud Light widened the company's reach into modules and active optical systems. By the time AI-networking demand became visible in the income statement, Lumentum had already spent years assembling the operating architecture needed to participate across more than one layer of the optical bill of materials.

## Downturn, Succession, and the Hurlston Era

The corporate arc bent downward before it bent up again. Fiscal 2024 revenue fell to $1,359.2 million from $1,767.0 million in fiscal 2023. The FY2024 annual report made clear that both end-market weakness and imaging-and-sensing normalization were pressing on the business at the same time. The post-acquisition platform existed, but the market it needed had not yet arrived in force. [FY2024 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1633978/000162828024038024/lite-20240629.htm)

The board responded with a CEO change announced on February 3, 2025 and effective February 7, 2025. Alan Lowe retired after leading Lumentum since the spin. Michael Hurlston took over after leading Synaptics and, before that, holding senior operating roles at Broadcom and then serving as chief executive of Finisar from January 2018 until that company was acquired in August 2019. The 2025 proxy said the board had run an extensive search and chose Hurlston because of his mix of public-company leadership in photonics and semiconductors. That made the succession look less like a generic turnaround hire and more like a sector-specific reset timed to a new product cycle. [Leadership transition release](https://investor.lumentum.com/financial-news-releases/news-details/2025/Lumentum-Announces-Leadership-Transition/default.aspx) [2025 proxy statement](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1633978/000130817925000615/lite014752-def14a.htm)

The timing turned out to be favorable. Fiscal 2025 revenue recovered to $1,645.0 million. By Q3 FY2026, quarterly revenue had reached a record $808.4 million, with components revenue at $533.3 million and systems revenue at $275.1 million. In other words, the decade-long build - spin-off, consumer-sensing scale, Oclaro, NeoPhotonics, Cloud Light, and then leadership change - finally produced an operating statement that read unmistakably as an AI-optics company rather than a more general photonics conglomerate. [Q4 FY2025 results](https://investor.lumentum.com/financial-news-releases/news-details/2025/Lumentum-Announces-Fourth-Quarter-and-Full-Fiscal-Year-2025-Results/default.aspx) [Q3 FY2026 results](https://investor.lumentum.com/financial-news-releases/news-details/2026/Lumentum-Announces-Third-Quarter-of-Fiscal-Year-2026-Financial-Results/default.aspx)

## A Capability Timeline, Not Just an M&A Timeline

Another way to read Lumentum's first decade was as a sequence of operating problems being solved one by one.

| Phase | Primary source evidence | What it added |
|---|---|---|
| 2015 spin | JDSU separation and Viavi rename | Standalone public-company shell and inherited optical-and-laser operations |
| 2017 sensing scale | VCSEL volume production for consumer 3D sensing | Ultra-high-volume emitter manufacturing and packaging discipline |
| 2018 Oclaro close | $1.8 billion transaction completed in December 2018 | Deeper indium-phosphide and coherent manufacturing capability |
| 2022 NeoPhotonics close | Higher-speed cloud and telecom optics stack | Additional coherent design depth and engineering talent |
| 2023 Cloud Light close | More than $200 million prior-12-month revenue and strong 800G mix | Finished modules, packaging and wider systems exposure |
| 2025-2026 ramp | Record components and systems revenue in fiscal 2026 | Proof that the earlier capability build could be monetized |

[FY2025 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1633978/000162828025040830/lite-20250628.htm) [Lumentum company timeline](https://www.lumentum.com/en/company) [Oclaro acquisition close](https://investor.lumentum.com/financial-news-releases/news-details/2018/Lumentum-Announces-Completion-Of-Oclaro-Acquisition-2018-12-10/default.aspx) [NeoPhotonics acquisition close](https://investor.lumentum.com/financial-news-releases/news-details/2022/Lumentum-Announces-Completion-of-NeoPhotonics-Acquisition/default.aspx) [Cloud Light announcement](https://investor.lumentum.com/financial-news-releases/news-details/2023/Lumentum-to-Acquire-Cloud-Light-to-Accelerate-Data-Center-Speed-and-Scalability/default.aspx) [Q3 FY2026 results](https://investor.lumentum.com/financial-news-releases/news-details/2026/Lumentum-Announces-Third-Quarter-of-Fiscal-Year-2026-Financial-Results/default.aspx)

What made the chronology important was that each step answered a different question. The spin-off answered whether the company could stand alone. Consumer 3D sensing answered whether it could manufacture photonics products at very high volume. Oclaro and NeoPhotonics answered whether it could control more of the InP and coherent stack. Cloud Light answered whether it would remain primarily a component supplier or move further into packaged interconnect. By fiscal 2026, the company was finally earning revenue from all of those answers at once.

The corporate history therefore did not read as a straight line from old telecom optics to AI. It read as an accumulation of adjacent capabilities that only later looked, in retrospect, like an AI-optics platform. That was why the fiscal 2024 trough and the fiscal 2026 rebound mattered so much together: the former exposed how expensive the build had been, while the latter showed what the build had actually been for.

That was the real reason the history chapter mattered. The company that entered fiscal 2026 was not simply the 2015 spin-off with better demand. It was the product of one manufacturing supercycle, three major capability extensions and a leadership reset that all occurred before the market fully rewarded the result. Lumentum's later AI-optics identity therefore rested on decisions made across almost the entire prior decade rather than on a sudden strategic break with its past.

chapters.title: Optical Communications, Commercial Lasers, and the cloud-and-datacenter inflection
chapters.body:
## Two Businesses, One Inflection Point

Lumentum's segment reporting by the frozen window told the story plainly. Cloud & Networking was the business absorbing AI and cloud spending; Industrial Tech was the business still carrying the after-effects of weaker sensing demand and a softer industrial cycle. In fiscal 2025, Cloud & Networking contributed $1,410.8 million of revenue and Industrial Tech contributed $234.2 million. A year earlier those figures had been $1,084.9 million and $274.3 million respectively. [FY2025 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1633978/000162828025040830/lite-20250628.htm)

| Fiscal year | Cloud & Networking | Industrial Tech | Total revenue |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| FY2023 | $1,322.5m | $444.5m | $1,767.0m |
| FY2024 | $1,084.9m | $274.3m | $1,359.2m |
| FY2025 | $1,410.8m | $234.2m | $1,645.0m |

The attraction of that table was not merely the rebound in the first column. It was the divergence. Cloud & Networking grew by $325.9 million in fiscal 2025 while Industrial Tech fell by another $40.1 million. The company was not recovering through a broad cyclical lift. It was recovering because one part of the portfolio was pulling decisively ahead of the other. [FY2025 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1633978/000162828025040830/lite-20250628.htm)

## Components and Systems: The Quarterly Mix Shift

The segment disclosure alone still understated the change, because by fiscal 2026 management had also begun framing the revenue base by product layer. The quarterly releases broke revenue into components and systems, which made visible how far Lumentum had moved beyond the older picture of a company selling only lasers and subsystems into someone else's module house. [Q1 FY2026 results](https://investor.lumentum.com/financial-news-releases/news-details/2025/Lumentum-Announces-First-Quarter-of-Fiscal-Year-2026-Financial-Results/default.aspx) [Q2 FY2026 results](https://investor.lumentum.com/financial-news-releases/news-details/2026/Lumentum-Announces-Second-Quarter-of-Fiscal-Year-2026-Financial-Results/default.aspx) [Q3 FY2026 results](https://investor.lumentum.com/financial-news-releases/news-details/2026/Lumentum-Announces-Third-Quarter-of-Fiscal-Year-2026-Financial-Results/default.aspx)

| Quarter | Components revenue | Systems revenue | Total revenue |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Q1 FY2026 | $379.2m | $154.6m | $533.8m |
| Q2 FY2026 | $474.6m | $190.9m | $665.5m |
| Q3 FY2026 | $533.3m | $275.1m | $808.4m |

That bridge mattered for interpretation. Components were still the larger business, but systems were rising faster in absolute dollars. Between Q1 and Q3 FY2026, components added $154.1 million of quarterly revenue while systems added $120.5 million. A company that had once been read mainly through EMLs, pumps and tunable lasers was now monetizing more of the packaging and finished-interconnect layer as well.

## Cloud & Networking: The Component Franchise

The cloud business was broader than the earlier draft sometimes suggested. Official product and investor materials showed it spanning high-speed EMLs, CW lasers, pump lasers, narrow-linewidth laser assemblies, coherent modules, pluggable transceivers, optical circuit switches and, increasingly, co-packaged-optics light sources. Lumentum's 100G PAM4 and 200G PAM4 EML pages explicitly positioned those devices for 800G and 1.6T transitions, while the company's tunable-laser portfolio and coherent-transceiver pages showed that the same segment still served datacenter interconnect, metro and long-haul optical transport. [EML 100G product page](https://www.lumentum.com/en/products/eml-100g-pam4-cwdm-laser) [EML 200G product page](https://www.lumentum.com/en/products/eml-200g-pam4-cwdm-laser) [Ultra-narrow linewidth nano-ITLA](https://www.lumentum.com/en/products/ultra-narrow-linewidth-nano-integrable-tunable-laser-assembly-nitla) [Coherent transceivers overview](https://www.lumentum.com/en/optical-communications/products/dwdm-and-coherent-optical-transceivers/coherent-transceivers)

Management's own quarter-by-quarter language reinforced that breadth. The Q4 FY2025 release said performance had been broad-based across the cloud-focused business, with particular strength in EML chips, pump lasers, narrow-linewidth laser assemblies and 800G modules. Q1 FY2026 then described record quarterly components revenue, driven by datacom lasers, coherent components and cloud transceiver demand. By Q3 FY2026, the release was again highlighting the same families rather than a single narrow product. The primary-source record therefore argued against a one-product reading of the AI ramp. [Q4 FY2025 results](https://investor.lumentum.com/financial-news-releases/news-details/2025/Lumentum-Announces-Fourth-Quarter-and-Full-Fiscal-Year-2025-Results/default.aspx) [Q1 FY2026 results](https://investor.lumentum.com/financial-news-releases/news-details/2025/Lumentum-Announces-First-Quarter-of-Fiscal-Year-2026-Financial-Results/default.aspx) [Q3 FY2026 results](https://investor.lumentum.com/financial-news-releases/news-details/2026/Lumentum-Announces-Third-Quarter-of-Fiscal-Year-2026-Financial-Results/default.aspx)

## Systems, Cloud Light, and the Move Up the Stack

Cloud Light broadened that stack materially. When Lumentum announced the acquisition in October 2023, it said the deal would deliver a more than five-fold expansion in its served cloud intra-data-center opportunity and that nearly all of Cloud Light's prior-12-month revenue had come from 400G or higher-speed transceivers. More than half of Cloud Light's most recent-quarter transceiver revenue had come from 800G modules. The strategic logic was plain: if AI networking was going to be won through finished optical interconnect as well as chips, Lumentum needed more of the module and assembly layer under its own roof. [Cloud Light announcement](https://investor.lumentum.com/financial-news-releases/news-details/2023/Lumentum-to-Acquire-Cloud-Light-to-Accelerate-Data-Center-Speed-and-Scalability/default.aspx)

The product pages showed what that meant in practice. Lumentum's 800G 2xDR4 OSFP module used silicon photonics with four 1311 nm CW DFB lasers. Its 800G ZR+ coherent pluggables combined indium phosphide photonic integrated circuits with silicon photonics. The commercial catalog also included a 1.6T 2xDR4 TRO OSFP module for AI and cloud data centers. Those were not research concepts. They were catalogued, specified products that placed the company directly in the finished-module conversation as well as in the upstream laser conversation. [800G 2xDR4 OSFP](https://www.lumentum.com/en/products/800g-2dr4-osfp-transceiver-module) [800G ZR+ coherent pluggables](https://www.lumentum.com/en/products/800g-zr-coherent-pluggable-transceivers) [1.6T 2xDR4 TRO OSFP](https://www.lumentum.com/products/16t-2dr4-tro-osfp-transceiver-module)

## OCS and CPO: The Next Layer of the Segment Story

The next layer up was optical circuit switching and co-packaged optics. On March 26, 2025, Lumentum announced that its R300 optical circuit switch was sampling with multiple hyperscale customers and was slated for general availability in the second half of 2025. By February 2026, Hurlston said OCS backlog had already moved well beyond $400 million, while the company had also received an incremental multi-hundred-million-dollar co-packaged-optics order deliverable in the first half of calendar 2027. Those were not speculative research vectors anymore; they had become order-book items. [R300 OCS release](https://investor.lumentum.com/financial-news-releases/news-details/2025/Lumentum-Optical-Circuit-Switch-to-Improve-Next-Generation-AI-Data-Center-Scalability/default.aspx) [Q2 FY2026 results](https://investor.lumentum.com/financial-news-releases/news-details/2026/Lumentum-Announces-Second-Quarter-of-Fiscal-Year-2026-Financial-Results/default.aspx)

The CPO product footprint was also more concrete than the old draft allowed. Lumentum's ELSFP external-laser-source module was designed for co-packaged optics. Its CW-laser pages explicitly discussed silicon-photonics transceivers and CPO architectures. OFC 2026 materials then showed super-high-power laser sources and multi-channel DWDM ultra-high-power laser sources for next-generation CPO designs. That was the segment expanding into a future architecture while still being paid by the current one. [ELSFP product page](https://www.lumentum.com/en/products/external-laser-source-els-module-ultra-high-power-laser) [CW lasers for SiPh transceivers](https://www.lumentum.com/en/products/data-center/cw-lasers/cw-lasers-sipho-transceivers) [OFC 2026 release](https://investor.lumentum.com/financial-news-releases/news-details/2026/Lumentum-Demonstrates-Industry-Leading-Technologies-and-Products-for-Scale-Out-Scale-Up-and-Scale-Across-AI-Infrastructure-at-OFC-2026/default.aspx)

## Industrial Tech: Smaller, but Not Empty

Industrial Tech was not a trivial residual bucket. It encompassed industrial lasers, semiconductor-processing lasers, 3D-sensing VCSELs and related photonics products. Revenue fell from $274.3 million in fiscal 2024 to $234.2 million in fiscal 2025, which made the segment numerically smaller and strategically secondary in the frozen-window story. But the official materials filled in more of that segment than the older chapter had. [FY2025 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1633978/000162828025040830/lite-20250628.htm)

At Photonics West 2026 the company highlighted next-generation ultrafast and UV laser platforms for precision manufacturing. At OFC 2026 it separately described a 1060 nm VCSEL scale-up platform built on an ultra-high-volume 3D-sensing manufacturing base that had shipped more than 10 billion emitters. That made Industrial Tech look less like a dead appendage and more like a slower-growing technology base whose manufacturing know-how still fed future products and architectural experiments. [Photonics West 2026 release](https://investor.lumentum.com/financial-news-releases/news-details/2026/Lumentum-Showcases-Next-Generation-Ultrafast-and-UV-Laser-Platforms-for-Precision-Manufacturing-at-Photonics-West-2026/default.aspx) [VCSEL scale-up release](https://investor.lumentum.com/financial-news-releases/news-details/2026/Lumentum-Showcases-Breakthrough-Optical-Scale-Up-Demonstration-at-OFC-2026-Using-VCSEL-Technology/default.aspx)

## Concentration and Geography: What the Segment Split Did Not Say

Lumentum's filings were unusually explicit about concentration even while anonymizing the customers. In fiscal 2025, Customer A represented 16.0 percent of total net revenue and Customer B 15.4 percent. In the first nine months of fiscal 2026, two customers individually accounted for 24 percent and 16 percent of total net revenue. The segment story therefore was not only about product breadth. It was also about the company's growing dependence on a very small number of large cloud buyers. [FY2025 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1633978/000162828025040830/lite-20250628.htm) [Q3 FY2026 10-Q](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001633978/000162828026030777/lite-20260328.htm)

The same caution applied to geography. Lumentum's FY2025 filing assigned revenue by the country where product was initially shipped, not by final end-market deployment. Hong Kong accounted for $398.6 million of fiscal 2025 revenue, Thailand for $291.8 million, the United States for $312.3 million and Mexico for $148.5 million. Those were real concentrations, but they were as much about logistics, contract manufacturing and shipping hubs as about final demand. That distinction mattered because it prevented the kind of overly precise customer mapping that the earlier draft had tried to make. [FY2025 10-K geography table](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1633978/000162828025040830/R115.htm) [FY2025 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1633978/000162828025040830/lite-20250628.htm)

By spring 2026, then, the segment picture resolved into two very different businesses: a Cloud & Networking segment that was compounding across components, systems, OCS and CPO; and an Industrial Tech segment whose revenues were smaller but whose manufacturing base still mattered technologically. The company no longer needed a speculative bridge between the two. The filings, product pages and trade-show releases supplied it.

## Telecom, DCI and Long-Haul Stayed Inside the Cloud Story

The Cloud & Networking segment was not only a hyperscale short-reach story. Lumentum's coherent-transceiver and tunable-laser materials showed that the same segment still served datacenter interconnect, metro and long-haul use cases. The 800G ZR+ pluggable page described hybrid photonic integrated circuits that combined indium phosphide and silicon photonics, while the nano-ITLA and other narrow-linewidth laser pages sat squarely in coherent transmission applications. In September 2024, the company, Marvell and Coherent also announced 800G ZR/ZR+ interoperability over links up to 500 kilometers. That meant the cloud segment still contained a real DCI and transport franchise, even as AI-cluster optics dominated the growth narrative. [800G ZR+ coherent pluggables](https://www.lumentum.com/en/products/800g-zr-coherent-pluggable-transceivers) [Ultra-narrow linewidth nano-ITLA](https://www.lumentum.com/en/products/ultra-narrow-linewidth-nano-integrable-tunable-laser-assembly-nitla) [Marvell-Lumentum-Coherent interoperability release](https://investor.lumentum.com/financial-news-releases/news-details/2024/Marvell-Lumentum-and-Coherent-Demonstrate-Industrys-First-800G-ZR-ZR-Pluggable-Modules-for-500km-Data-Center-Interconnects/default.aspx)

That mattered because it changed how to think about diversification inside the segment. The same reporting bucket held short-reach datacenter optics, cloud modules, coherent DCI parts and more traditional networking products. The question for investors was therefore not whether Cloud & Networking was diversified in a textbook sense. It was whether the faster-growing cloud layers were becoming large enough that the slower telecom and DCI layers turned into ballast rather than drag.

## A Product Map, Not Just a Segment Label

A product map made that easier to see.

| Product family | Segment | Evidence in primary sources | Main use case by frozen window |
|---|---|---|---|
| 100G and 200G EMLs | Cloud & Networking | Product pages and earnings releases | 800G and 1.6T optical engines |
| CW lasers and ELS | Cloud & Networking | SiPh and CPO product pages | Silicon-photonics modules and future CPO |
| 800G 2xDR4 module | Cloud & Networking | Commercial product page | AI and cloud short-reach interconnect |
| 800G ZR+ coherent pluggables | Cloud & Networking | Commercial product page and interop demo | DCI, metro and cloud edge transport |
| R300 OCS | Cloud & Networking | March 2025 product release | Hyperscale optical switching fabrics |
| Ultrafast and UV laser platforms | Industrial Tech | Photonics West 2026 release | Precision manufacturing and semiconductor processing |
| VCSEL scale-up platform | Industrial Tech with cloud adjacency | March 2026 VCSEL release | Alternative AI scale-up interconnect path |

[EML 100G product page](https://www.lumentum.com/en/products/eml-100g-pam4-cwdm-laser) [EML 200G product page](https://www.lumentum.com/en/products/eml-200g-pam4-cwdm-laser) [ELSFP product page](https://www.lumentum.com/en/products/external-laser-source-els-module-ultra-high-power-laser) [800G 2xDR4 OSFP](https://www.lumentum.com/en/products/800g-2dr4-osfp-transceiver-module) [R300 OCS release](https://investor.lumentum.com/financial-news-releases/news-details/2025/Lumentum-Optical-Circuit-Switch-to-Improve-Next-Generation-AI-Data-Center-Scalability/default.aspx) [Photonics West 2026 release](https://investor.lumentum.com/financial-news-releases/news-details/2026/Lumentum-Showcases-Next-Generation-Ultrafast-and-UV-Laser-Platforms-for-Precision-Manufacturing-at-Photonics-West-2026/default.aspx) [VCSEL scale-up release](https://investor.lumentum.com/financial-news-releases/news-details/2026/Lumentum-Showcases-Breakthrough-Optical-Scale-Up-Demonstration-at-OFC-2026-Using-VCSEL-Technology/default.aspx)

The value of that map was that it made the segment divergence more concrete. Cloud & Networking was not one datacenter part. It was a layered optical franchise spanning component, module and systems categories. Industrial Tech, meanwhile, was smaller in revenue terms but still housed platforms that mattered technologically. That was why the post-trough recovery looked asymmetric rather than binary: one segment was carrying the income statement, while the other still supplied know-how and optionality.

chapters.title: FY2024 $1.36B trough, FY2025 recovery, and the cloud-and-datacenter mix shift
chapters.body:
## The Anatomy of a Trough

Fiscal 2024 was the year in which Lumentum's earlier revenue model broke down in the income statement. Net revenue fell to $1,359.2 million from $1,767.0 million in fiscal 2023. The company attributed the decline to lower sales in Cloud & Networking and Industrial Tech alike, with particular weakness in telecom and imaging-and-sensing demand. The downturn was broad enough that it showed up not only in the top line but in factory absorption, profitability and the write-downs that followed. [FY2024 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1633978/000162828024038024/lite-20240629.htm) [Q4 FY2024 results](https://investor.lumentum.com/financial-news-releases/news-details/2024/Lumentum-Announces-Fourth-Quarter-and-Full-Fiscal-Year-2024-Results/default.aspx)

## Revenue Trajectory: FY2018 to FY2025

| Fiscal year | Net revenue | YoY change |
|---|---:|---:|
| FY2018 | $1,247.7m | -- |
| FY2019 | $1,565.3m | +25.5% |
| FY2020 | $1,678.6m | +7.2% |
| FY2021 | $1,742.8m | +3.8% |
| FY2022 | $1,712.6m | -1.7% |
| FY2023 | $1,767.0m | +3.2% |
| FY2024 | $1,359.2m | -23.1% |
| FY2025 | $1,645.0m | +21.0% |

The earlier climb from FY2018 through FY2021 captured the combined effect of consumer 3D-sensing scale, telecom demand and the Oclaro integration. The later plateau in FY2022 and FY2023 now read as transitional rather than stable. By the time revenue collapsed in FY2024, Lumentum had already completed the NeoPhotonics acquisition and was carrying a broader technology stack into a much weaker market. [FY2020 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1633978/000163397820000011/lumentumfy20-10k.htm) [FY2024 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1633978/000162828024038024/lite-20240629.htm) [FY2025 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1633978/000162828025040830/lite-20250628.htm)

## Annual Profitability: The GAAP and Non-GAAP Split

The margin history explained why the stock's recovery had to be earned. On a full-year basis, Lumentum's published metrics showed a business that had fallen much further on a GAAP basis than topline investors sometimes remembered, then only partially repaired itself in fiscal 2025 even before the fiscal 2026 acceleration. [Q4 FY2024 results](https://investor.lumentum.com/financial-news-releases/news-details/2024/Lumentum-Announces-Fourth-Quarter-and-Full-Fiscal-Year-2024-Results/default.aspx) [Q4 FY2025 results](https://investor.lumentum.com/financial-news-releases/news-details/2025/Lumentum-Announces-Fourth-Quarter-and-Full-Fiscal-Year-2025-Results/default.aspx)

| Fiscal year | GAAP gross margin | Non-GAAP gross margin | GAAP operating margin | Non-GAAP operating margin |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| FY2023 | 32.2% | 43.2% | -6.5% | 19.2% |
| FY2024 | 18.5% | 33.0% | -31.9% | 2.8% |
| FY2025 | 28.0% | 34.7% | -10.9% | 9.7% |

That table made two points. First, fiscal 2024 was not merely a soft year. It was a year of severe operating deleverage and charges. Second, fiscal 2025 was a recovery year, but not yet a full one on a GAAP basis. The market's later enthusiasm in fiscal 2026 was therefore built on the belief that the non-GAAP trajectory would keep converting into cleaner reported earnings as utilization improved and one-off charges faded.

## Why Fiscal 2024 Broke So Hard

The pressure on margins was straightforward. Lumentum still carried the fixed-cost structure of a company with fabs in Japan, the United States and the United Kingdom, plus large assembly and test operations in Thailand, while revenue in legacy telecom and sensing lines was falling sharply. The FY2024 filing tied the decline to weaker product volumes and lower factory absorption. The Q4 FY2024 release then added more specific damage: full-year results included a $35.8 million write-off tied to discontinuation of the internally developed digital-signal-processor and radio-frequency integrated-circuit program and a $139.8 million valuation allowance against deferred tax assets. [FY2024 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1633978/000162828024038024/lite-20240629.htm) [Q4 FY2024 results](https://investor.lumentum.com/financial-news-releases/news-details/2024/Lumentum-Announces-Fourth-Quarter-and-Full-Fiscal-Year-2024-Results/default.aspx)

In that sense, the trough was both cyclical and self-clearing. Cyclical, because telecom and imaging demand had weakened sharply. Self-clearing, because management was forced to abandon projects and cost structures that no longer matched the demand environment. The later recovery in margins therefore did not require a return to the old business mix; it required a better one.

## The Quarter-by-Quarter Recovery

The quarterly releases showed the operating recovery in unusually clean sequence. Revenue and margins improved quarter after quarter through fiscal 2025 and then accelerated further in the first three quarters of fiscal 2026. [Q1 FY2025 results](https://investor.lumentum.com/financial-news-releases/news-details/2024/Lumentum-Announces-Fiscal-First-Quarter-2025-Financial-Results/) [Q2 FY2025 results](https://investor.lumentum.com/financial-news-releases/news-details/2025/Lumentum-Announces-Fiscal-Second-Quarter-2025-Financial-Results/default.aspx) [Q3 FY2025 results](https://investor.lumentum.com/financial-news-releases/news-details/2025/Lumentum-Announces-Fiscal-Third-Quarter-2025-Financial-Results/default.aspx) [Q4 FY2025 results](https://investor.lumentum.com/financial-news-releases/news-details/2025/Lumentum-Announces-Fourth-Quarter-and-Full-Fiscal-Year-2025-Results/default.aspx) [Q1 FY2026 results](https://investor.lumentum.com/financial-news-releases/news-details/2025/Lumentum-Announces-First-Quarter-of-Fiscal-Year-2026-Financial-Results/default.aspx) [Q2 FY2026 results](https://investor.lumentum.com/financial-news-releases/news-details/2026/Lumentum-Announces-Second-Quarter-of-Fiscal-Year-2026-Financial-Results/default.aspx) [Q3 FY2026 results](https://investor.lumentum.com/financial-news-releases/news-details/2026/Lumentum-Announces-Third-Quarter-of-Fiscal-Year-2026-Financial-Results/default.aspx)

| Quarter | Revenue | Non-GAAP gross margin | Non-GAAP operating margin |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Q1 FY2025 | $336.9m | 32.8% | 3.0% |
| Q2 FY2025 | $402.2m | 32.3% | 7.9% |
| Q3 FY2025 | $425.2m | 35.2% | 10.8% |
| Q4 FY2025 | $480.7m | 37.8% | 15.0% |
| Q1 FY2026 | $533.8m | 39.4% | 18.7% |
| Q2 FY2026 | $665.5m | 42.5% | 25.2% |
| Q3 FY2026 | $808.4m | 47.9% | 32.2% |

That progression was the operating heart of the Lumentum re-rating. By Q3 FY2026, quarterly revenue was nearly 2.4 times the Q1 FY2025 trough-adjacent level, while non-GAAP operating margin had risen by almost 29 percentage points. The improvement was too sustained to dismiss as a one-quarter shortage squeeze. It reflected mix, utilization, pricing discipline and a business that was finally filling the manufacturing base it had assembled.

## Capital Structure and the Refinancing Bridge

The draft's description of the debt stack also needed tightening. Lumentum's FY2025 and FY2026 filings showed that the 0.50% Convertible Senior Notes due 2026 remained part of the capital structure, but the more important frozen-window development was what management did about them. In September 2025, Lumentum issued $1,265.0 million of 0.375% Convertible Senior Notes due 2032. At the same time, it used about $843.1 million of the proceeds to repurchase $581.1 million principal amount of the 2026 notes. That was not a cosmetic refinancing. It materially reduced the near-dated maturity overhang that had hung over the trough period. [FY2026 Q1 10-Q](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1633978/000162828025049073/lite-20250927.htm) [FY2026 Q2 10-Q](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001633978/000162828026005129/lite-20251227.htm)

Liquidity changed meaningfully as the cloud business accelerated. Total cash, cash equivalents and short-term investments stood at $877.1 million at the end of fiscal 2025, rose to $1,121.8 million at the end of Q1 FY2026, $1,155.3 million at the end of Q2 FY2026, and then jumped to $3,172.3 million at the end of Q3 FY2026 after the March 2026 preferred-stock issuance tied to the NVIDIA strategic partnership. What had been a cyclical balance-sheet story became a funded capacity-expansion story within three quarters. [Q4 FY2025 results](https://investor.lumentum.com/financial-news-releases/news-details/2025/Lumentum-Announces-Fourth-Quarter-and-Full-Fiscal-Year-2025-Results/default.aspx) [Q1 FY2026 results](https://investor.lumentum.com/financial-news-releases/news-details/2025/Lumentum-Announces-First-Quarter-of-Fiscal-Year-2026-Financial-Results/default.aspx) [Q2 FY2026 results](https://investor.lumentum.com/financial-news-releases/news-details/2026/Lumentum-Announces-Second-Quarter-of-Fiscal-Year-2026-Financial-Results/default.aspx) [Q3 FY2026 results](https://investor.lumentum.com/financial-news-releases/news-details/2026/Lumentum-Announces-Third-Quarter-of-Fiscal-Year-2026-Financial-Results/default.aspx)

## Hurlston's Strategic Reframe

Michael Hurlston did not take over in the middle of fiscal 2024; the board announced the succession on February 3, 2025 and made it effective February 7, 2025. That mattered because it placed the handoff not at the trough's onset but just before the recovery became visible in the reported numbers. Hurlston inherited a business that had already bought Oclaro, NeoPhotonics and Cloud Light; his task was to convert those assets into a more cloud-centered earnings profile. [Leadership transition release](https://investor.lumentum.com/financial-news-releases/news-details/2025/Lumentum-Announces-Leadership-Transition/default.aspx) [2025 proxy statement](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1633978/000130817925000615/lite014752-def14a.htm)

That reframing showed up in the numbers before it showed up in the long-form narrative. Fiscal 2025 Cloud & Networking revenue was $1,410.8 million against $234.2 million for Industrial Tech. Q1 FY2026, Q2 FY2026 and Q3 FY2026 then added the product-type confirmation: components and systems were both rising, and management was talking not only about EMLs and 800G modules but about OCS and co-packaged optics as additional growth engines. The trough, in short, had not proved the asset base was wrong. It had proved that the monetization path ran through AI-cloud optics rather than through a simple telecom snapback. [FY2025 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1633978/000162828025040830/lite-20250628.htm) [Q1 FY2026 results](https://investor.lumentum.com/financial-news-releases/news-details/2025/Lumentum-Announces-First-Quarter-of-Fiscal-Year-2026-Financial-Results/default.aspx) [Q2 FY2026 results](https://investor.lumentum.com/financial-news-releases/news-details/2026/Lumentum-Announces-Second-Quarter-of-Fiscal-Year-2026-Financial-Results/default.aspx) [Q3 FY2026 results](https://investor.lumentum.com/financial-news-releases/news-details/2026/Lumentum-Announces-Third-Quarter-of-Fiscal-Year-2026-Financial-Results/default.aspx)

## Cash Flow, Working Capital and Capital Intensity

The annual cash-flow statement showed that the operating repair was real but initially lagged the accounting recovery. Cash provided by operating activities was $179.8 million in fiscal 2023, fell to $24.7 million in fiscal 2024 and then recovered to $126.3 million in fiscal 2025. That was a meaningful improvement, but it still showed how much of the fiscal 2025 recovery was being absorbed by working capital and investment requirements rather than dropping cleanly to cash. [FY2025 10-K cash flow discussion](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1633978/000162828025040830/lite-20250628.htm) [FY2025 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1633978/000162828025040830/lite-20250628.htm)

Management's own discussion explained why. In fiscal 2025, inventories rose by $71.3 million to support market demand, accounts receivable increased by $58.7 million with higher revenue, and prepayments and other current and non-current assets rose by $35.1 million, mainly from value-added-tax receivables driven by capital expenditures and inventory purchases. At the same time, capital expenditures were $231.0 million. The company was not simply enjoying a recovery. It was funding one. [FY2025 10-K cash flow discussion](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1633978/000162828025040830/lite-20250628.htm)

The fiscal 2026 year-to-date numbers suggested that the quality of earnings was improving as scale returned. In the first six months of fiscal 2026, net cash provided by operating activities was $184.6 million versus $63.9 million in the prior-year period. By the first nine months of fiscal 2026, that figure had risen to $388.4 million versus $62.3 million in the comparable prior period. The income statement recovery was therefore beginning to convert into cash more decisively by the frozen window. [FY2026 Q2 10-Q](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001633978/000162828026005129/lite-20251227.htm) [FY2026 Q3 10-Q](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001633978/000162828026030777/lite-20260328.htm)

## The Charge Stack in Fiscal 2025

Fiscal 2025 also looked cleaner once the non-recurring items were spelled out. The 10-K said the year included a $34.9 million gain on sale of a facility in Shenzhen, $12.2 million of legal and professional fees tied primarily to non-ordinary-course legal matters, $6.2 million of CEO transition costs and a $3.2 million bad-debt reserve related to remaining unpaid balances due from Huawei associated with trade restrictions. It also recorded a $2.7 million write-off of in-process R&D assets for projects the company would no longer pursue. Those details mattered because they showed a business still absorbing the after-effects of prior strategic choices even as the core cloud mix improved. [FY2025 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1633978/000162828025040830/lite-20250628.htm)

That was also why the non-GAAP and GAAP stories diverged so much. Non-GAAP operating margin captured the real utilization and mix recovery. GAAP still carried amortization of acquired intangibles, write-offs, legal settlements, facility dispositions and transition costs from the decade-long build-out. For a company that had grown by acquisition and then been forced through a trough, that gap was economically meaningful rather than cosmetic.

## Balance-Sheet Repair Changed the Optionality

The combination of recovering operating cash flow, the 2032-convert refinancing and the NVIDIA preferred investment changed the balance-sheet discussion. During fiscal 2025, cash and cash equivalents rose to $520.7 million from $436.7 million, while short-term investments were $356.4 million, taking the combined liquidity position to $877.1 million. By Q3 FY2026, cash, cash equivalents and short-term investments had reached $3.17 billion. That scale of liquidity did not guarantee execution, but it did remove the old question of whether Lumentum would be forced to choose between balance-sheet defense and capacity expansion. [FY2025 10-K cash and investments](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1633978/000162828025040830/lite-20250628.htm) [Q3 FY2026 results](https://investor.lumentum.com/financial-news-releases/news-details/2026/Lumentum-Announces-Third-Quarter-of-Fiscal-Year-2026-Financial-Results/default.aspx)

By the frozen window, then, the financial deep dive read as a three-step story. Fiscal 2024 showed the full cost of underutilization and write-downs. Fiscal 2025 showed revenue and margin recovery, but still with meaningful working-capital drag and residual charges. Fiscal 2026 began to show what the company looked like once scale, cash generation and financing capacity started to align. That was when the earlier acquisitions began to look less like expensive history and more like funded operating leverage.

## Acquisition Accounting Never Really Went Away

One reason the reported earnings took longer than the commercial recovery to normalize was that the acquisition legacy remained large in the P&L. The 10-K said Lumentum recorded $149.7 million of amortization related to intangible assets in fiscal 2025, after $150.6 million in fiscal 2024 and $127.7 million in fiscal 2023. It also said fiscal 2024 abnormal excess-capacity charges reflected a near-term reduction in manufacturing production driven by a non-recurring inventory-reduction effort after the pandemic-era supply-chain disruption and factory consolidation efforts. Those details explained why the company could look commercially better before it looked fully clean on a GAAP basis. [FY2025 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1633978/000162828025040830/lite-20250628.htm)

chapters.title: Post-Hurlston quarters and the cloud-and-datacenter trajectory
chapters.body:
## From Trough to Inflection

The earnings story after the trough was much cleaner in the primary sources than in the original draft. The company did not move from stagnation straight to the March 2026 NVIDIA announcement. It climbed there quarter by quarter, and the official releases show the sequence clearly. [Q1 FY2025 results](https://investor.lumentum.com/financial-news-releases/news-details/2024/Lumentum-Announces-Fiscal-First-Quarter-2025-Financial-Results/) [Q2 FY2025 results](https://investor.lumentum.com/financial-news-releases/news-details/2025/Lumentum-Announces-Fiscal-Second-Quarter-2025-Financial-Results/default.aspx) [Q3 FY2025 results](https://investor.lumentum.com/financial-news-releases/news-details/2025/Lumentum-Announces-Fiscal-Third-Quarter-2025-Financial-Results/default.aspx) [Q4 FY2025 results](https://investor.lumentum.com/financial-news-releases/news-details/2025/Lumentum-Announces-Fourth-Quarter-and-Full-Fiscal-Year-2025-Results/default.aspx)

## Lowe's Final Quarters

Q1 FY2025, reported on November 7, 2024, brought revenue of $336.9 million and non-GAAP gross margin of 32.8 percent. Alan Lowe said the company had set a new record for datacom laser-chip orders, including substantial 200G EML orders, and pointed explicitly to strong demand from multiple customers including an AI infrastructure customer. That is a more precise and more defensible way to describe the inflection than the draft's broader language about unnamed hyperscaler programs. [Q1 FY2025 results](https://investor.lumentum.com/financial-news-releases/news-details/2024/Lumentum-Announces-Fiscal-First-Quarter-2025-Financial-Results/)

Q2 FY2025, reported on February 6, 2025, lifted revenue further to $402.2 million with non-GAAP gross margin of 32.3 percent and non-GAAP operating margin of 7.9 percent. The same week, on February 3, the board announced that Hurlston would take over as chief executive effective February 7. The timing matters: the board changed CEOs after the first clear quarter of order acceleration, but before the margin recovery was fully visible. [Q2 FY2025 results](https://investor.lumentum.com/financial-news-releases/news-details/2025/Lumentum-Announces-Fiscal-Second-Quarter-2025-Financial-Results/default.aspx) [Leadership transition release](https://investor.lumentum.com/financial-news-releases/news-details/2025/Lumentum-Announces-Leadership-Transition/default.aspx)

## Hurlston's First Reported Quarters

Hurlston's first full earnings release as chief executive came on May 6, 2025 for Q3 FY2025. Revenue reached $425.2 million, non-GAAP gross margin improved to 35.2 percent, and non-GAAP operating margin reached 10.8 percent. He framed the company as being positioned for AI data-center scaling and emphasized advanced EMLs and ultra-high-power lasers rather than legacy telecom products. [Q3 FY2025 results](https://investor.lumentum.com/financial-news-releases/news-details/2025/Lumentum-Announces-Fiscal-Third-Quarter-2025-Financial-Results/default.aspx)

Q4 FY2025, reported on August 12, 2025, was the quarter in which the growth thesis became visible even to a skeptical reader of press releases. Revenue rose to $480.7 million and non-GAAP gross margin to 37.8 percent. Hurlston said the outperformance was broad-based across the cloud-focused business, with particular strength in EML chips, pump lasers, narrow-linewidth laser assemblies for data-center interconnect, and 800G modules. He also said the company had enough confidence in demand to target quarterly revenue above $600 million by June 2026 or earlier. [Q4 FY2025 results](https://investor.lumentum.com/financial-news-releases/news-details/2025/Lumentum-Announces-Fourth-Quarter-and-Full-Fiscal-Year-2025-Results/default.aspx)

| Quarter | Revenue | Non-GAAP gross margin | Non-GAAP operating margin |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Q1 FY2025 | $336.9m | 32.8% | 3.0% |
| Q2 FY2025 | $402.2m | 32.3% | 7.9% |
| Q3 FY2025 | $425.2m | 35.2% | 10.8% |
| Q4 FY2025 | $480.7m | 37.8% | 15.0% |
| Q1 FY2026 | $533.8m | 39.4% | 18.7% |
| Q2 FY2026 | $665.5m | 42.5% | 25.2% |
| Q3 FY2026 | $808.4m | 47.9% | 32.2% |

## FY2026: Additional Growth Engines Enter the Story

The November 4, 2025 Q1 FY2026 release showed that revenue acceleration was not stopping at 800G modules. Revenue was $533.8 million, with $379.2 million of components revenue and $154.6 million of systems revenue. Hurlston said the results and forward guidance reflected strong momentum across data center, data-center interconnect and long-haul markets, but he also stressed that two major growth engines - optical circuit switches and co-packaged optics - had not yet contributed meaningfully. [Q1 FY2026 results](https://investor.lumentum.com/financial-news-releases/news-details/2025/Lumentum-Announces-First-Quarter-of-Fiscal-Year-2026-Financial-Results/default.aspx)

By Q2 FY2026, reported on February 3, 2026, those growth engines were becoming much more concrete. Revenue reached $665.5 million, non-GAAP gross margin hit 42.5 percent, and Hurlston said OCS backlog had moved well beyond $400 million. He also disclosed an incremental multi-hundred-million-dollar order in co-packaged optics, deliverable in the first half of calendar 2027. The company was now speaking in the language of backlog and committed programs rather than only design activity. [Q2 FY2026 results](https://investor.lumentum.com/financial-news-releases/news-details/2026/Lumentum-Announces-Second-Quarter-of-Fiscal-Year-2026-Financial-Results/default.aspx)

## NVIDIA and the Balance-Sheet Step-Change

On March 2, 2026, NVIDIA and Lumentum announced multiyear strategic agreements under which NVIDIA would make a $2 billion investment in Lumentum, accompanied by a multibillion-dollar purchase commitment and future capacity access rights for advanced laser components. The language in both companies' releases was unusually specific about the use of proceeds: support R&D, future capacity and operations as Lumentum built out U.S.-based manufacturing capabilities in a new fab. [NVIDIA-Lumentum partnership](https://investor.lumentum.com/financial-news-releases/news-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Strategic-Partnership-With-Lumentum-to-Develop-State-of-the-Art-Optics-Technology/default.aspx)

The follow-on announcement on March 26, 2026 filled in the site-level detail. Lumentum said it would establish a new U.S. manufacturing facility in Greensboro, North Carolina, that the site was already operational and would be retrofitted to make indium-phosphide-based CW and ultra-high-power lasers, and that the project would preserve and create more than 400 U.S. manufacturing jobs. NVIDIA was identified as a customer of the facility. [Greensboro facility release](https://investor.lumentum.com/financial-news-releases/news-details/2026/Lumentum-Announces-New-U-S--Manufacturing-Facility-to-Produce-Advanced-Lasers-for-the-Worlds-Largest-AI-Data-Centers/default.aspx)

## Q3 FY2026: The Record Quarter

The May 5, 2026 Q3 FY2026 release was the strongest single checkpoint inside the frozen window. Revenue rose 90 percent year on year to a record $808.4 million. Non-GAAP gross margin rose to 47.9 percent and non-GAAP operating margin to 32.2 percent. Components revenue was $533.3 million and systems revenue $275.1 million. Total cash, cash equivalents and short-term investments reached $3,172.3 million, primarily because of the March preferred-stock issuance. [Q3 FY2026 results](https://investor.lumentum.com/financial-news-releases/news-details/2026/Lumentum-Announces-Third-Quarter-of-Fiscal-Year-2026-Financial-Results/default.aspx)

Just as important, the release gave a cleaner operating explanation than the draft's unsupported scarcity rhetoric. Hurlston said margin improvement had been driven by operational rigor, pricing discipline and product mix, and that the quarter's mix was helped by strength in laser chips as well as by pump lasers and narrow-linewidth laser assemblies. He also said key growth drivers - co-packaged optics and optical circuit switches - were beginning to contribute. That is a narrower claim than saying the company was effectively sold out through 2027, but it is the claim the company actually put on the record. [Q3 FY2026 results](https://investor.lumentum.com/financial-news-releases/news-details/2026/Lumentum-Announces-Third-Quarter-of-Fiscal-Year-2026-Financial-Results/default.aspx)

The external markers also accumulated. S&P Dow Jones Indices said Lumentum would join the S&P 500 before the market opened on March 23, 2026, and the company later said it would join the Nasdaq-100 Index on May 11, 2026. Those events did not prove the durability of the earnings ramp, but they did show how quickly the market's view of the company had changed. [S&P 500 inclusion](https://investor.lumentum.com/financial-news-releases/news-details/2026/Lumentum-to-Join-the-SP-500-Index/default.aspx) [Nasdaq-100 inclusion](https://www.lumentum.com/en/company)

The earnings story through May 23, 2026 therefore reads less like a single AI-stock epiphany than like a disciplined staircase: Q1 FY2025 record laser-chip orders, Q2 FY2025 higher revenue, Q3 and Q4 FY2025 clear margin recovery under a new CEO, Q1 FY2026 proof that components and systems were both scaling, Q2 FY2026 backlog and CPO commitments, and Q3 FY2026 a balance sheet and income statement transformed by the NVIDIA transaction and the underlying demand ramp.


## The Scorecard the Company Itself Set

The cleanest way to read the earnings story was as a rolling scorecard of revenue and margin expansion.

| Quarter | Revenue | Non-GAAP gross margin | Non-GAAP operating margin |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Q1 FY2025 | $336.9m | 32.8% | 3.0% |
| Q2 FY2025 | $402.2m | 32.3% | 7.9% |
| Q3 FY2025 | $425.2m | 35.2% | 10.8% |
| Q4 FY2025 | $480.7m | 37.8% | 15.0% |
| Q1 FY2026 | $533.8m | 39.4% | 18.7% |
| Q2 FY2026 | $665.5m | 42.5% | 25.2% |
| Q3 FY2026 | $808.4m | 47.9% | 32.2% |

[Q1 FY2025 results](https://investor.lumentum.com/financial-news-releases/news-details/2024/Lumentum-Announces-Fiscal-First-Quarter-2025-Financial-Results/) [Q2 FY2025 results](https://investor.lumentum.com/financial-news-releases/news-details/2025/Lumentum-Announces-Fiscal-Second-Quarter-2025-Financial-Results/default.aspx) [Q3 FY2025 results](https://investor.lumentum.com/financial-news-releases/news-details/2025/Lumentum-Announces-Fiscal-Third-Quarter-2025-Financial-Results/default.aspx) [Q4 FY2025 results](https://investor.lumentum.com/financial-news-releases/news-details/2025/Lumentum-Announces-Fourth-Quarter-and-Full-Fiscal-Year-2025-Results/default.aspx) [Q1 FY2026 results](https://investor.lumentum.com/financial-news-releases/news-details/2025/Lumentum-Announces-First-Quarter-of-Fiscal-Year-2026-Financial-Results/default.aspx) [Q2 FY2026 results](https://investor.lumentum.com/financial-news-releases/news-details/2026/Lumentum-Announces-Second-Quarter-of-Fiscal-Year-2026-Financial-Results/default.aspx) [Q3 FY2026 results](https://investor.lumentum.com/financial-news-releases/news-details/2026/Lumentum-Announces-Third-Quarter-of-Fiscal-Year-2026-Financial-Results/default.aspx)

That table explained why the Q3 FY2026 release mattered so much. It did not merely report another strong quarter. It capped seven consecutive quarters of revenue growth and a sustained widening in operating margin. The shape of the recovery was sequential, not episodic.

## The Marker for the Next Quarter

The company also ended the frozen window having set a very explicit near-term test for itself. On the May 5, 2026 Q3 release, Lumentum guided the June-quarter revenue range to $960 million to $1.01 billion with non-GAAP operating margin of 35 percent to 36 percent. That guidance mattered because it was strong enough that a miss would have reset the narrative quickly, while a beat or clean in-line print would have reinforced the idea that the AI-optics ramp was still broadening rather than plateauing. [Q3 FY2026 results](https://investor.lumentum.com/financial-news-releases/news-details/2026/Lumentum-Announces-Third-Quarter-of-Fiscal-Year-2026-Financial-Results/default.aspx)

chapters.title: Hurlston, Wajid Ali CFO, and the Herscher-chaired board
chapters.body:
## A Franchise in Transition

Lumentum's leadership chapter only made sense once the dates were corrected. Michael Hurlston was not appointed in February 2024. The board announced the transition on February 3, 2025 and made it effective February 7, 2025. That was the first CEO change in Lumentum's history as a standalone public company, and the 2025 proxy made plain that the board treated it as a full strategic handoff rather than a routine succession. [Leadership transition release](https://investor.lumentum.com/financial-news-releases/news-details/2025/Lumentum-Announces-Leadership-Transition/default.aspx) [2025 proxy statement](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1633978/000130817925000615/lite014752-def14a.htm)

The proxy's letter from Hurlston and independent chair Penelope Herscher framed fiscal 2025 as the year in which Lumentum had entered the AI-optics mainstream with "clarity, discipline, and a renewed focus on execution." That language was not empty investor-relations varnish. The board had already spent much of the prior year absorbing the telecom downturn, integrating Cloud Light, and deciding that the next chief executive needed direct photonics experience and transformation credibility. [2025 proxy statement](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1633978/000130817925000615/lite014752-def14a.htm)

## Michael Hurlston: A Sector-Specific Appointment

The official record gave a much richer biography than the draft's earlier shorthand. Hurlston held a B.S. and M.S. in Electrical Engineering and an M.B.A., all from the University of California, Davis. He spent November 2001 to October 2017 at Broadcom, rising through senior operating and sales roles. He then became chief executive of Finisar in January 2018 and remained there until August 2019, when he moved to Synaptics as president and chief executive officer. That meant Lumentum was not hiring an adjacent semiconductor manager and hoping he would learn optics; it was hiring a chief executive who had already run one of the industry's defining optical-component peers. [Leadership transition release](https://investor.lumentum.com/financial-news-releases/news-details/2025/Lumentum-Announces-Leadership-Transition/default.aspx) [2025 proxy statement](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1633978/000130817925000615/lite014752-def14a.htm)

That Finisar interval mattered strategically. Broadcom gave Hurlston high-volume silicon discipline; Finisar gave him direct experience with optical modules, components, and hyperscale-related demand; Synaptics gave him a recent case study in portfolio repositioning and margin repair. The board said in the proxy that it had conducted an extensive search with an executive recruitment team and unanimously concluded that Hurlston was the right chief executive for what it called a critical and exciting period. The reasoning, as disclosed, was not generalized executive polish but his mix of public-company leadership in photonics and semiconductors and his view of the future of the global photonics industry. [2025 proxy statement](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1633978/000130817925000615/lite014752-def14a.htm)

By the frozen window the performance under that appointment was already material. Fiscal 2025 revenue rose to $1,645.0 million from $1,359.2 million in fiscal 2024. Q1 FY2026 revenue reached $533.8 million, Q2 reached $665.5 million, and Q3 reached a record $808.4 million. That revenue staircase makes the succession easier to evaluate: Hurlston inherited the company just before the recovery became visible and then spent the next five reported quarters attaching operating discipline and new capacity language to it. [Q4 FY2025 results](https://investor.lumentum.com/financial-news-releases/news-details/2025/Lumentum-Announces-Fourth-Quarter-and-Full-Fiscal-Year-2025-Results/default.aspx) [Q1 FY2026 results](https://investor.lumentum.com/financial-news-releases/news-details/2025/Lumentum-Announces-First-Quarter-of-Fiscal-Year-2026-Financial-Results/default.aspx) [Q2 FY2026 results](https://investor.lumentum.com/financial-news-releases/news-details/2026/Lumentum-Announces-Second-Quarter-of-Fiscal-Year-2026-Financial-Results/default.aspx) [Q3 FY2026 results](https://investor.lumentum.com/financial-news-releases/news-details/2026/Lumentum-Announces-Third-Quarter-of-Fiscal-Year-2026-Financial-Results/default.aspx)

## The CFO Anchor: Wajid Ali Since 2019

The continuity story ran through Wajid Ali. The 2025 proxy said Ali had joined Lumentum as executive vice president and chief financial officer in February 2019 after serving in the same role at Synaptics from May 2015 to February 2019. Earlier roles included vice president and controller at Teledyne Technologies, chief financial officer of DALSA, and finance posts at AMD and ATI.
