[FY2025 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1633978/000162828025040830/lite-20250628.htm) [Greensboro facility release](https://investor.lumentum.com/financial-news-releases/news-details/2026/Lumentum-Announces-New-U-S--Manufacturing-Facility-to-Produce-Advanced-Lasers-for-the-Worlds-Largest-AI-Data-Centers/default.aspx)

## 4. Product-Transition Risk: 800G to 1.6T, OCS, and CPO

The fourth risk is that the company was trying to scale several product transitions at once. The 800G 2xDR4 OSFP, 800G ZR+ coherent pluggables, 1.6T TRO module, optical circuit switches and co-packaged-optics light sources all belonged to the forward story, but they were at different stages of maturity. Some were commercial catalog items, some were early sampling platforms, and some were backlog or order-book narratives whose full revenue conversion still lay ahead. [800G 2xDR4 OSFP](https://www.lumentum.com/en/products/800g-2dr4-osfp-transceiver-module) [1.6T 2xDR4 TRO OSFP](https://www.lumentum.com/products/16t-2dr4-tro-osfp-transceiver-module) [R300 OCS release](https://investor.lumentum.com/financial-news-releases/news-details/2025/Lumentum-Optical-Circuit-Switch-to-Improve-Next-Generation-AI-Data-Center-Scalability/default.aspx)

That mix creates a classic execution risk. If 800G pricing softens before 1.6T volumes are fully mature, or if OCS and CPO ramps take longer to monetize than the order language suggests, the operating-leverage story can look less linear than it did at the Q3 FY2026 peak. The company itself implicitly acknowledged that risk when Q1 FY2026 said OCS and CPO were not yet meaningful contributors and Q3 FY2026 said those growth drivers were beginning to kick in. [Q1 FY2026 results](https://investor.lumentum.com/financial-news-releases/news-details/2025/Lumentum-Announces-First-Quarter-of-Fiscal-Year-2026-Financial-Results/default.aspx) [Q3 FY2026 results](https://investor.lumentum.com/financial-news-releases/news-details/2026/Lumentum-Announces-Third-Quarter-of-Fiscal-Year-2026-Financial-Results/default.aspx)

## 5. Integration, Financing, and Balance-Sheet Complexity

The fifth risk is that Lumentum's growth narrative still sat on top of several unfinished financial and integration threads. Cloud Light was closed in November 2023, yet the Q3 FY2026 release still discussed escrow settlement, related legal costs, and a non-GAAP adjustment tied to a $27.5 million settlement outcome. The same release also recorded acquisition-related costs for another business acquired in March 2026. This is not a sign of distress, but it is a reminder that the company was still digesting deals while selling itself as a clean AI-optics beneficiary. [Q3 FY2026 results](https://investor.lumentum.com/financial-news-releases/news-details/2026/Lumentum-Announces-Third-Quarter-of-Fiscal-Year-2026-Financial-Results/default.aspx)

Financing added its own complications. The 2026 notes overhang from the trough period was partly addressed in September 2025 through the issuance of $1.265 billion of 2032 converts and the repurchase of $581.1 million principal amount of 2026 notes. Then, in March 2026, the NVIDIA partnership introduced $2 billion of preferred-stock capital. Each of those steps improved liquidity and capacity options; each also made the capital structure more layered and more sensitive to execution. [FY2026 Q1 10-Q](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1633978/000162828025049073/lite-20250927.htm) [FY2026 Q2 10-Q](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001633978/000162828026005129/lite-20251227.htm) [NVIDIA-Lumentum partnership](https://investor.lumentum.com/financial-news-releases/news-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Strategic-Partnership-With-Lumentum-to-Develop-State-of-the-Art-Optics-Technology/default.aspx)

## 6. Telecom and Industrial Tech Still Mattered

The sixth risk is that the non-AI parts of the portfolio had not disappeared; they had merely become smaller. Industrial Tech revenue fell from $444.5 million in fiscal 2023 to $274.3 million in fiscal 2024 and then to $234.2 million in fiscal 2025. The company's own releases still talked about long-haul and broader networking markets alongside cloud and AI. That mix was useful as diversification, but it also meant Lumentum remained partly exposed to slower-recovering telecom budgets and to industrial cycles that did not move in step with hyperscale optics. [FY2025 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1633978/000162828025040830/lite-20250628.htm) [Q1 FY2026 results](https://investor.lumentum.com/financial-news-releases/news-details/2025/Lumentum-Announces-First-Quarter-of-Fiscal-Year-2026-Financial-Results/default.aspx)

The company did show continuing technical activity in those areas. OFC 2025 materials highlighted long-haul networking products and 800G ZR/ZR+ coherent modules. Photonics West 2026 highlighted ultrafast, UV and 3D-sensing laser products. But the frozen-window evidence still supports a hierarchy in which those businesses were supporting actors rather than coequal growth engines. [OFC 2025 showcase release](https://investor.lumentum.com/financial-news-releases/news-details/2025/Lumentum-to-Showcase-Cutting-Edge-Optical-Innovations-for-Cloud-AI-and-Networking-Infrastructure-at-OFC-2025/default.aspx) [Photonics West 2026 release](https://investor.lumentum.com/financial-news-releases/news-details/2026/Lumentum-Showcases-Next-Generation-Ultrafast-and-UV-Laser-Platforms-for-Precision-Manufacturing-at-Photonics-West-2026/default.aspx)

## The Risk Picture After the Re-Rating

The net effect of those six risks is not that the thesis broke. It is that the company traded one set of problems for another. The trough-era risk was cyclical collapse in telecom and sensing. The post-recovery risk was concentration around AI customers, AI-networking product ramps, and a manufacturing footprint concentrated in a few critical places.

That is still a better risk set than the one Lumentum faced in fiscal 2024. The company had more liquidity, more backlog, more visible product breadth, and a clearer leadership structure. But it was also more tightly wound into a handful of cloud customers and into a supply chain whose fragility the company itself described in unusual detail. That is why the risk chapter still matters even after the revenue line turned sharply upward. [FY2025 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1633978/000162828025040830/lite-20250628.htm) [Q2 FY2026 results](https://investor.lumentum.com/financial-news-releases/news-details/2026/Lumentum-Announces-Second-Quarter-of-Fiscal-Year-2026-Financial-Results/default.aspx) [Q3 FY2026 results](https://investor.lumentum.com/financial-news-releases/news-details/2026/Lumentum-Announces-Third-Quarter-of-Fiscal-Year-2026-Financial-Results/default.aspx)


## 7. Footprint and Manufacturing-Execution Risk

A further risk sat inside the manufacturing map itself. As of June 28, 2025, Lumentum owned about 1,173,000 square feet of manufacturing space in Thailand and 472,000 square feet of manufacturing and R&D space in Japan, while also reporting that a single contract manufacturer accounted for 25.1 percent of total net inventory purchases. The company had deliberately shifted production out of the Shenzhen facility and into Thailand, but that concentration meant that execution, tariffs, partner performance and local disruption could all hit the same revenue engine at once. [FY2025 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1633978/000162828025040830/lite-20250628.htm) [2025 annual report PDF](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1633978/000130817925000617/lite014752-ars.pdf)

## 8. Capital-Allocation Risk After the Re-Rating

The balance sheet looked far stronger by Q3 FY2026, but that introduced a different risk: capital allocation. Fiscal 2025 capital expenditures were $231.0 million, inventories rose by $71.3 million to support demand, and the March 2026 NVIDIA preferred investment gave management still more room to expand. The risk was no longer one of immediate liquidity stress. It was whether Lumentum would invest the enlarged balance sheet into capacity and programs that converted into durable returns rather than into the kind of overbuild that optical suppliers had experienced in earlier cycles. [FY2025 10-K cash flow discussion](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1633978/000162828025040830/lite-20250628.htm) [Q3 FY2026 results](https://investor.lumentum.com/financial-news-releases/news-details/2026/Lumentum-Announces-Third-Quarter-of-Fiscal-Year-2026-Financial-Results/default.aspx)

chapters.title: 1.6T scaling, Hurlston operational restructuring, and the FY2027 horizon
chapters.body:
## The 800G Ramp Had Matured Into a Broader AI-Optics Story

By late May 2026, the question was no longer whether Lumentum had found real demand. The first three quarters of fiscal 2026 had already answered that. Revenue went from $533.8 million in Q1 to $665.5 million in Q2 and $808.4 million in Q3, while non-GAAP operating margin climbed from 18.7 percent to 25.2 percent and then 32.2 percent. What mattered for the outlook was whether that trajectory was widening into a multi-product platform or simply running hot on a narrow part of the optical cycle. [Q1 FY2026 results](https://investor.lumentum.com/financial-news-releases/news-details/2025/Lumentum-Announces-First-Quarter-of-Fiscal-Year-2026-Financial-Results/default.aspx) [Q2 FY2026 results](https://investor.lumentum.com/financial-news-releases/news-details/2026/Lumentum-Announces-Second-Quarter-of-Fiscal-Year-2026-Financial-Results/default.aspx) [Q3 FY2026 results](https://investor.lumentum.com/financial-news-releases/news-details/2026/Lumentum-Announces-Third-Quarter-of-Fiscal-Year-2026-Financial-Results/default.aspx)

The official materials argued for the broader-platform reading. Q1 FY2026 said optical circuit switches and co-packaged optics had not yet contributed meaningfully, which meant the revenue base was still dominated by earlier cloud products. Q2 FY2026 then disclosed that OCS backlog had moved beyond $400 million and that an incremental multi-hundred-million-dollar CPO order had been booked for delivery in the first half of calendar 2027. Q3 FY2026 said those growth drivers were beginning to kick in. That sequence mattered because it suggested the outlook was no longer resting only on 800G pluggables and related laser content. [Q1 FY2026 results](https://investor.lumentum.com/financial-news-releases/news-details/2025/Lumentum-Announces-First-Quarter-of-Fiscal-Year-2026-Financial-Results/default.aspx) [Q2 FY2026 results](https://investor.lumentum.com/financial-news-releases/news-details/2026/Lumentum-Announces-Second-Quarter-of-Fiscal-Year-2026-Financial-Results/default.aspx) [Q3 FY2026 results](https://investor.lumentum.com/financial-news-releases/news-details/2026/Lumentum-Announces-Third-Quarter-of-Fiscal-Year-2026-Financial-Results/default.aspx)

## Hurlston's Operational Restructuring

The outlook chapter also needed a cleaner read on restructuring. The draft was right that Hurlston moved quickly, but the primary sources were more specific than the generalized prose had been. The Q1 FY2026 release said restructuring charges primarily related to a reduction in force intended to enhance operational efficiency and realign investment toward the most critical initiatives. The Q2 FY2026 release reported a net reversal of $0.4 million in restructuring charges because severance and wind-down costs were lower than estimated. The Q3 FY2026 release again referred to a reduction in force for operational efficiency and prioritization. [Q1 FY2026 results](https://investor.lumentum.com/financial-news-releases/news-details/2025/Lumentum-Announces-First-Quarter-of-Fiscal-Year-2026-Financial-Results/default.aspx) [Q2 FY2026 results](https://investor.lumentum.com/financial-news-releases/news-details/2026/Lumentum-Announces-Second-Quarter-of-Fiscal-Year-2026-Financial-Results/default.aspx) [Q3 FY2026 results](https://investor.lumentum.com/financial-news-releases/news-details/2026/Lumentum-Announces-Third-Quarter-of-Fiscal-Year-2026-Financial-Results/default.aspx)

That mattered for the outlook because it linked margin expansion to management action rather than only to favorable mix. A company could enjoy a scarcity boom without becoming structurally better run. The evidence in the releases suggested Lumentum was trying to do both at once: raising utilization with demand while also narrowing costs around the businesses management believed would matter most in 2026 and 2027.

## 1.6T as the Nearest Product Bridge

The 1.6T roadmap sat at the center of the forward case because it was the nearest large product transition that clearly extended the current cloud narrative. Lumentum's commercial catalog already included the 1.6T 2xDR4 TRO OSFP transceiver, described as an eight-lane 212.5 Gbps PAM4 module for AI and cloud data centers with typical power consumption of 16 watts. That was not slideware. It was a product the company was prepared to describe in commercial detail. [1.6T 2xDR4 TRO OSFP](https://www.lumentum.com/products/16t-2dr4-tro-osfp-transceiver-module)

At the same time, OFC 2026 showed where management wanted the lane-speed story to go next. The company said it would demonstrate a 1.6T DR4 OSFP prototype built around four 400G differential EMLs as a stepping-stone to 3.2T. That was important because it showed the 1.6T outlook in two layers: a nearer-term commercial TRO module and a more forward-looking differential-EML architecture. The likely implication for fiscal 2027 was that 1.6T would become not one product but a family of increasingly differentiated interconnect options. [OFC 2026 release](https://investor.lumentum.com/financial-news-releases/news-details/2026/Lumentum-Demonstrates-Industry-Leading-Technologies-and-Products-for-Scale-Out-Scale-Up-and-Scale-Across-AI-Infrastructure-at-OFC-2026/default.aspx)

## OCS and CPO as New Revenue Legs

If 1.6T was the cleanest extension of today's revenue base, OCS and CPO were the biggest sources of upside and uncertainty. The March 2025 R300 announcement made clear that Lumentum already had an optical circuit switch product in sampling, not merely in concept development. Q2 FY2026 then translated that into backlog language exceeding $400 million. That mattered because it showed the OCS story had moved from technical promise to financial visibility. [R300 OCS release](https://investor.lumentum.com/financial-news-releases/news-details/2025/Lumentum-Optical-Circuit-Switch-to-Improve-Next-Generation-AI-Data-Center-Scalability/default.aspx) [Q2 FY2026 results](https://investor.lumentum.com/financial-news-releases/news-details/2026/Lumentum-Announces-Second-Quarter-of-Fiscal-Year-2026-Financial-Results/default.aspx)

Co-packaged optics moved in parallel. Lumentum's ELSFP product page, CW-laser pages, OFC 2026 release and the NVIDIA partnership all pointed in the same direction: the company wanted to be the laser and light-source supplier inside future CPO systems, not merely a bystander to them. The incremental multi-hundred-million-dollar CPO order disclosed in Q2 FY2026, along with the Greensboro manufacturing announcement later that spring, made that ambition more concrete. [ELSFP product page](https://www.lumentum.com/en/products/external-laser-source-els-module-ultra-high-power-laser) [CW lasers for SiPh transceivers](https://www.lumentum.com/en/products/data-center/cw-lasers/cw-lasers-sipho-transceivers) [NVIDIA-Lumentum partnership](https://investor.lumentum.com/financial-news-releases/news-details/2026/NVIDIA-Announces-Strategic-Partnership-With-Lumentum-to-Develop-State-of-the-Art-Optics-Technology/default.aspx) [Greensboro facility release](https://investor.lumentum.com/financial-news-releases/news-details/2026/Lumentum-Announces-New-U-S--Manufacturing-Facility-to-Produce-Advanced-Lasers-for-the-Worlds-Largest-AI-Data-Centers/default.aspx)

## Capacity and Capital Were No Longer the Immediate Constraint

A large part of the forward case therefore sat inside manufacturing execution. The March 2026 Greensboro announcement said the company would retrofit an operational North Carolina site to produce InP-based CW and ultra-high-power lasers and would invest hundreds of millions of dollars over the next several years. Combined with the July 2024 purchase of the Sagamihara wafer-fab site and the existing Thailand-centered assembly network, that pointed to a company still aligning its manufacturing footprint with what it believed demand would require. [Greensboro facility release](https://investor.lumentum.com/financial-news-releases/news-details/2026/Lumentum-Announces-New-U-S--Manufacturing-Facility-to-Produce-Advanced-Lasers-for-the-Worlds-Largest-AI-Data-Centers/default.aspx) [FY2025 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1633978/000162828025040830/lite-20250628.htm)

The balance sheet gave the company room to pursue that plan. By Q3 FY2026, cash, cash equivalents and short-term investments were $3,172.3 million, up sharply because of the Series A preferred stock issued in March 2026. Earlier, the company had also refinanced part of the 2026 convert overhang with the September 2025 2032 notes offering. From an outlook perspective, that mattered because capacity expansion at Lumentum no longer looked like a cash-strapped hope. It looked like a financed operating program. [Q3 FY2026 results](https://investor.lumentum.com/financial-news-releases/news-details/2026/Lumentum-Announces-Third-Quarter-of-Fiscal-Year-2026-Financial-Results/default.aspx) [FY2026 Q1 10-Q](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1633978/000162828025049073/lite-20250927.htm)

## What Had to Be True Next

By the frozen window, the forward markers the company itself had set were fairly concrete.

| Marker | Frozen-window evidence | Why it mattered next |
|---|---|---|
| Current demand durability | Q3 FY2026 revenue of $808.4m and Q4 guide of $960m-$1.01bn | Tested whether the revenue ramp was continuing into fiscal year-end |
| 1.6T conversion | Catalogued 1.6T products and OFC 2026 prototype demos | Determined whether 800G momentum could bridge into the next cycle |
| OCS monetization | Backlog beyond $400m | Showed whether a new system-level business could become material |
| CPO adoption | Incremental multi-hundred-million-dollar order for 1H CY2027 delivery | Indicated whether future optical architectures were moving into booked demand |
| Manufacturing follow-through | Greensboro retrofit plus Sagamihara and Thailand footprint | Determined whether Lumentum could supply the growth it was signaling |

[Q3 FY2026 results](https://investor.lumentum.com/financial-news-releases/news-details/2026/Lumentum-Announces-Third-Quarter-of-Fiscal-Year-2026-Financial-Results/default.aspx) [1.6T 2xDR4 TRO OSFP](https://www.lumentum.com/products/16t-2dr4-tro-osfp-transceiver-module) [OFC 2026 release](https://investor.lumentum.com/financial-news-releases/news-details/2026/Lumentum-Demonstrates-Industry-Leading-Technologies-and-Products-for-Scale-Out-Scale-Up-and-Scale-Across-AI-Infrastructure-at-OFC-2026/default.aspx) [Greensboro facility release](https://investor.lumentum.com/financial-news-releases/news-details/2026/Lumentum-Announces-New-U-S--Manufacturing-Facility-to-Produce-Advanced-Lasers-for-the-Worlds-Largest-AI-Data-Centers/default.aspx)

That framing kept the outlook grounded. It avoided pretending the company had already won every future optical architecture, but it also avoided reducing the story to a single 800G shortage cycle. By May 2026, Lumentum had already proven the current cloud ramp, had partial financial visibility into OCS and CPO, had a commercial and developmental 1.6T roadmap, and had both the financing and facility plans to push capacity further. The remaining uncertainty was no longer whether there was an opportunity. It was how much of that opportunity the company could convert into durable earnings before concentration, pricing or execution pushed back.

## Telecom and Industrial Tech Were Supportive, Not Leading

The non-cloud businesses still shaped the horizon, but more as stabilizers than as lead growth drivers. Q1 FY2026 spoke of strength across data center, data-center interconnect and long-haul markets, which suggested some recovery in the broader networking portfolio. Lumentum's OFC 2025 materials also highlighted 800G ZR/ZR+ and long-haul networking products, reinforcing that coherent and DCI remained live parts of the business even if they were no longer the central equity story. [Q1 FY2026 results](https://investor.lumentum.com/financial-news-releases/news-details/2025/Lumentum-Announces-First-Quarter-of-Fiscal-Year-2026-Financial-Results/default.aspx) [OFC 2025 showcase release](https://investor.lumentum.com/financial-news-releases/news-details/2025/Lumentum-to-Showcase-Cutting-Edge-Optical-Innovations-for-Cloud-AI-and-Networking-Infrastructure-at-OFC-2025/default.aspx)

Industrial Tech looked even less likely to drive the near-term outlook numerically, but it still provided technical optionality. Photonics West 2026 highlighted ultrafast and UV laser platforms plus a broad 3D-sensing VCSEL portfolio. The March 2026 VCSEL scale-up release also showed that the old sensing base could feed new AI interconnect ideas. That did not turn Industrial Tech into a coequal growth engine, but it did keep it from being a dead appendix in the medium-term thesis. [Photonics West 2026 release](https://investor.lumentum.com/financial-news-releases/news-details/2026/Lumentum-Showcases-Next-Generation-Ultrafast-and-UV-Laser-Platforms-for-Precision-Manufacturing-at-Photonics-West-2026/default.aspx) [VCSEL scale-up release](https://investor.lumentum.com/financial-news-releases/news-details/2026/Lumentum-Showcases-Breakthrough-Optical-Scale-Up-Demonstration-at-OFC-2026-Using-VCSEL-Technology/default.aspx)

## The Durability Question

The dossier still ended on a durability question rather than on a solved conclusion. The structural argument for Lumentum was compelling: every recent step up in AI-cluster density had required more optical content, not less, and the company now participated across components, modules, switching and prospective CPO light sources. But the risk argument remained real as well. A small number of customers still carried a very large share of revenue, and the operating footprint remained concentrated enough that execution could matter as much as demand. [FY2025 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1633978/000162828025040830/lite-20250628.htm) [Q3 FY2026 10-Q](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001633978/000162828026030777/lite-20260328.htm)

That was why the most serious outlook reading, as of the frozen window, was neither euphoric nor skeptical by default. It was conditional. If 1.6T qualified on time, if OCS backlog converted, if CPO orders broadened, and if the Thailand-Japan-US footprint scaled without major disruption, then fiscal 2026 could look like the start of a longer earnings base rather than the peak of a shortage-driven burst. The sources did not prove that outcome. They did show that, by May 2026, Lumentum had finally assembled enough product breadth, funding and manufacturing intent for the question to be worth asking in earnest.

A successful next chapter, as the primary sources framed it, would not simply mean another quarter of elevated revenue. It would mean the company proved three things in sequence: that current AI demand remained durable enough to absorb new capacity; that 1.6T, OCS and CPO converted from demos and backlog into recognized revenue; and that customer concentration eased at least somewhat as the addressable product set widened. If those conditions held, the fiscal 2026 surge could become a base rather than a spike. If they did not, the same concentration and capital-intensity that now looked like strengths could begin to look cyclical again. [Q3 FY2026 results](https://investor.lumentum.com/financial-news-releases/news-details/2026/Lumentum-Announces-Third-Quarter-of-Fiscal-Year-2026-Financial-Results/default.aspx) [FY2025 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1633978/000162828025040830/lite-20250628.htm)

That conditionality was what kept the outlook analysis from collapsing into either cheerleading or backward-looking caution. The sources supported a company that had become substantially stronger, better financed and more strategically important by late May 2026. They did not support pretending that optical cycles had stopped being cyclical. The next phase of the story still depended on disciplined execution through the very growth categories that had just transformed the franchise.

financials.fiscal_year_end: End of June (year ending late June/early July)
financials.key_finding: Lumentum's fiscal 2024 (year ending June 2024) revenue was approximately $1.36B — compressed from the post-Apple-VCSEL peak; the FY2025-FY2026 trajectory has reflected the cloud-and-datacenter scaling on 800G transceiver volume at hyperscaler customers while the telecom segment has stabilised off the post-cycle bottom.
structural_observations: The fiscal 2024 trough reflects post-Apple-VCSEL normalisation plus the broader 2023-2024 telecom market downturn.
Cloud-and-datacenter category (800G transceivers at hyperscalers) is the principal forward growth lever post-Hurlston succession.
Indium phosphide vertical integration (from December 2018 Oclaro acquisition) provides structural competitive advantage given limited merchant InP capacity globally.
NeoPhotonics acquisition (August 2022) brought coherent transceiver IP.
Customer base spans hyperscalers (cloud), telecom OEMs (cycle), and the Apple legacy.

leadership.key_finding: Lumentum's leadership is defined by the February 2024 CEO transition from Alan Lowe (founder-CEO from the 2015 JDSU spin-off) to Michael Hurlston (former Synaptics CEO; earlier Broadcom General Manager). Lowe's nine-year tenure delivered the original spin-off through the Oclaro acquisition and the Apple 3D-sensing scaling and then the telecom downturn; Hurlston's mandate is the cloud-and-datacenter pivot toward the 800G and 1.6T transceiver opportunity. The executive team layers Hurlston's strategic refocus with continuity at the CFO function under Wajid Ali (since 2019) and broad operating leadership across the optical communications and commercial laser segments. The board is chaired by Independent Chair Penny Herscher (former CEO of FirstRain and Simplex Solutions, broad EDA/SaaS governance experience) and includes long-tenured directors plus more recent additions calibrated to the AI-data-centre business profile.

ceo.framing: Hurlston joined Lumentum in February 2024 succeeding founder-CEO Alan Lowe. The Synaptics CEO tenure (2019-2024) involved the strategic refocus of the company away from PC/mobile touch toward IoT and edge AI; the Broadcom Mobile Connectivity GM background brought the high-volume mixed-signal product execution discipline. At Lumentum the strategic mandate is the cloud-and-datacenter pivot toward the 800G and 1.6T transceiver opportunity at hyperscaler customers, leveraging the post-NeoPhotonics coherent technology base. The UC Davis EE pedigree combined with the multi-decade Broadcom and Synaptics public-company operating experience produces the optical-communications-industry operating depth that the company needs to compete against the Coherent (COHR) and Marvell-Inphi competitive set.

board_of_directors.career: Former CEO of FirstRain (acquired by Ignite Technologies 2017); former CEO of Simplex Solutions (acquired by Cadence 2002); earlier senior leadership at Synopsys
board_of_directors.framing: Herscher brings EDA-industry CEO experience plus SaaS-CEO governance perspective. The Simplex Solutions and FirstRain CEO tenures span the semiconductor-tools and enterprise-SaaS categories; the Synopsys background brings the deep EDA-tools-industry perspective. The Independent Chair role at Lumentum during the CEO transition and the strategic refocus provides governance continuity.

board_of_directors.name: Harold L. Covert
board_of_directors.framing: Covert is a long-tenured technology-industry CFO veteran (formerly CFO at Openwave, Silicon Image, multiple other public technology companies) who provides audit-committee-grade finance governance. The director role includes lead audit committee responsibilities.

board_of_directors.name: Pamela Fletcher
board_of_directors.framing: Fletcher is the former Vice President of Global Innovation at General Motors and the former CEO of Delta Air Lines' Mileage Plus loyalty programme. The cross-industry technology and operations experience brings broader board perspective beyond the optical components industry.

board_of_directors.name: Brian Lillie
board_of_directors.framing: Lillie is the former Chief Product and Technology Officer of Equinix; the data centre and cloud infrastructure operating experience provides direct relevance to Lumentum's cloud-and-datacenter customer category. The Equinix tenure included the period of substantial cloud and interconnect infrastructure scaling that defines Lumentum's customer base.

board_of_directors.name: Janet Liang
board_of_directors.framing: Liang brings healthcare-industry operating experience and broader corporate governance perspective. The Kaiser Permanente leadership tenure provides large-organisation operating context.

board_of_directors.name: Bruce Robertson
board_of_directors.framing: Robertson is a venture capital industry veteran (Managing Director at H&Q Asia Pacific) and brings investor-perspective governance plus broader technology-industry pattern recognition. The venture capital experience spans multiple semiconductor and optical-component industry cycles.

leadership.board_composition_observation: Lumentum's board pairs Independent Chair Herscher (EDA/SaaS CEO experience) and CEO Hurlston with directors who bring relevant operational and industry depth: Covert for technology-industry CFO governance, Fletcher for cross-industry operating perspective, Lillie for data centre and cloud infrastructure operating context (the most directly relevant single director profile to the current strategic refocus), Liang for healthcare-industry governance, and Robertson for venture-capital and broader technology-industry cycle pattern recognition. The composition reflects the company's evolving business profile — cloud-and-datacenter optical components plus the legacy telecom and commercial laser exposure — and provides the governance bandwidth for the CEO-transition-era strategic refocus toward the AI infrastructure opportunity. The Lillie data-centre operating experience is the most strategically calibrated single director choice for the current period.
